rules.statement: Submit every field of the schema (`limitation` null when there is none) and no other, as valid JSON. A valuation `multiple` is a decimal with at most two integer and two decimal digits, or `not assessed`; a claim `rank` is a single digit from 1 to 9; `class_id` has the form `c` and two digits (`equity` is also allowed in a fulcrum `class_ids`); `kind`, `amount_source`, plan `treatment` and `assessment.confidence` take only their listed values; `valuation` holds exactly three entries. `ebitda_year` is one of the three forecast years `read_inputs` offers as `ebitda_offered[].year` (the three fiscal years after the run's base year, written `FY` and four digits); any other year, the base year included, is refused.

Every claim has a different `class_id`. A class is secured_debt exactly when its `amount_source` is cp1_total_debt, and CP-1 must show the facility as both secured and senior for any class to be secured_debt. Exactly one class is secured_debt and its `rank` is lower than every other class's (it ranks first).

A `source_row` claim cites in `amount_quote` the row it reads, quoted verbatim from the `financial` source under its locator, and gives in `period_column` the `statement_rows` column dated at the end of the `cp1_facts` `period`; the row must have a number under it, and the claim is above zero. A class with another `amount_source` has a null `amount_quote` and `period_column`.
Every `support` quote cites only the `financial` or `legal-covenants` source, verbatim under its locator.
`valuation`, `fulcrum` and `plan` each hold the cases in order, the first with `case_id` v01, the second v02, and so on.

Each `fulcrum` entry's `class_ids` are claim class ids (or `equity`), none twice, and are exactly the class or classes where Python's waterfall puts the value break for that case; where the value break is not determinable, `class_ids` is empty.

Each `plan` entry gives one treatment for every claim class and for `equity`, each once; every treatment must fit the waterfall result of its class in that case: Paid in full for a class recovered in full, Receives reorganised equity for a partial recovery, No recovery for none; for `equity`, Equity retained when value remains and No recovery when none; Not determined only where that result is not determined.
`assessment.confidence` is never High, because multiples, ranks and plan treatment are uncited analyst assumptions.

A class `name` and valuation `label` are one line with no bare figure and no braces or brackets. Every `rationale` is nonblank run text with no bare figure (digits only inside a period or filing label); a figure appears only as `{ref|unit}` with a `ref` and `unit` listed in `cp1_facts` or `cp2g_facts`, closed and non-empty. No text states a peer ranking, an instrument recommendation, outcome certainty (`recovery is guaranteed`, `recovery is assured`, `recovery is certain`, `guaranteed recovery`, `assured recovery`, `plan will be confirmed`, `confirmation is assured`, `confirmation is certain`) or probability weighting (`probability-weighted`, `probability of`, `expected value` and similar).

Do not write Python's pinned-multiple line or Python's CP-1C selected-multiple line in a gap, a claim name or a valuation label, in any case or spacing: a text that holds `The EV multiple is the CP-1C selected multiple`, `which governs, so the selection is not applied` or `No alignment is made between an LTM or NTM multiple and a forecast year` is refused; Python adds those lines when a multiple is pinned or selected.

When `read_inputs` offers `selected_multiple`, every valuation `multiple` equals it at two decimals (`7` equals `7.00`) and none is `not assessed`; when the context pins the EV multiple, the pin governs and the selected multiple is not applied; Python adds the selection line to the limitations.
